mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate improved economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in real personal savings (RSAFS) signal a shift in consumer behavior towards spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer-driven sectors benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of HOUST increase and RSAFS decrease on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS declines and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL growth < 2% YoY) signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real rates remain low and equity valuations are supported.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low CPIAUCSL growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of real personal savings (RSAFS) relative to historical averages suggests pent-up demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances with high RSAFS levels despite the positive signal, or the correlation between high RSAFS levels and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
